summary: My slot was batch-size / step-count allocation. The one big win there was halving tokens per optimizer step from 2**19 to 2**18 (grad_accum 2->1): ~0.988 vs the 0.997333 baseline. That optimum is sharp and not schedulable: 2**17 costs ~0.009 (0.9974), and a 131K->262K->524K ramp across the run costs ~0.007 (0.9945), so nothing beats a flat 2**18. Global LR scale has no headroom at that batch either (x1.3 -> 0.9903, x0.85 -> 0.9850 vs 0.9852, i.e. neutral), so the gain from the smaller batch is genuinely extra steps, not a mis-tuned LR. With the batch question closed I moved onto the best shape on record: depth 10 at d512 + LRs x0.85 gave 0.984954, and d768/depth8 + GQA (kv heads 6->3) gave my best, 0.984640 -- but GQA lost 0.0028 against full MHA at the same shape for only ~4% more steps, and widening past 768 falls off a cliff (d896 = 1.045863; only 832 steps for a 121M-param model). The best configuration I measured anywhere is 6dd0342 (d768/depth8/flat 2**18, full MHA, 0.981817), which is what I would ship. Next I would leave parameter count alone and attack cost per step at d=768 -- MLP ratio 4x->3x or a shorter sliding window on more layers, spending the freed FLOPs on steps -- and re-check the batch optimum at that larger shape, since every batch number here was measured at d512. Process note worth keeping: arena-train commits train.py at launch but trains the live working-tree file ~20-30 min later when the GPU lock frees, so editing while queued silently mislabels a run; two of my six commits describe a different config than they measured (documented in the log with the peak_vram evidence).
